title: 2.2 Taxonomy and Classification
description: Principles of biological classification, taxonomic hierarchy, and binomial nomenclature

questions.question: What is the scientific study of naming, describing, and classifying organisms called?
questions.explanation: Taxonomy is the branch of biology concerned with naming, describing, and classifying organisms into groups.

questions.question: Why is classification of living organisms important?
options: To organize organisms into groups for easier study and identification
To increase the number of species
To change the names of organisms
questions.correctAnswer: To organize organisms into groups for easier study and identification
questions.explanation: Classification helps biologists organize, study, and identify the millions of species on Earth systematically.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of the taxonomic hierarchy from most broad to most specific?
options: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Phylum, Kingdom, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.correctAnswer: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: The taxonomic hierarchy from broadest to most specific is: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of modern taxonomy?
questions.explanation: Carl Linnaeus developed the system of binomial nomenclature and hierarchical classification still used today.

questions.question: What is binomial nomenclature?
options: A naming system using only the species name
A naming system using three names
A two-part naming system consisting of genus and species
A naming system based on common names
questions.correctAnswer: A two-part naming system consisting of genus and species
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature gives every species a two-part scientific name: the genus name (capitalized) and the species name (lowercase).

questions.question: In binomial nomenclature, how should the scientific name of an organism be written?
options: Both genus and species in lowercase
Genus capitalized, species in lowercase, both italicized or underlined
questions.correctAnswer: Genus capitalized, species in lowercase, both italicized or underlined
questions.explanation: The genus name is capitalized, the species name is lowercase, and both are italicized or underlined in print.

questions.question: What is the correct way to write the scientific name of humans?
questions.explanation: Homo is capitalized, sapiens is lowercase, and both should be italicized: Homo sapiens.

questions.question: Which taxonomic rank is the most specific and includes only one type of organism?
questions.explanation: Species is the most specific and narrowest taxonomic rank, referring to a group of organisms that can interbreed.

questions.question: Which taxonomic rank is broader than family but narrower than class?
questions.explanation: The hierarchy places Order between Class and Family: Kingdom > Phylum > Class > Order > Family > Genus > Species.

questions.question: Organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring belong to the same:
questions.explanation: A species is defined as a group of organisms capable of interbreeding to produce fertile offspring.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of giving organisms scientific names?
options: To provide a universal name recognized worldwide regardless of language
questions.correctAnswer: To provide a universal name recognized worldwide regardless of language
questions.explanation: Scientific names are universal, avoiding confusion that arises from different common names in different languages and regions.

questions.question: In the scientific name Panthera leo, what does Panthera represent?
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first word (capitalized) is the genus; the second word (lowercase) is the species.

questions.question: How many kingdoms are there in the five-kingdom classification system?
questions.explanation: The five-kingdom classification system by Whittaker includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

questions.question: Which kingdom contains prokaryotic organisms?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms (bacteria) that lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

questions.question: What is the basic unit of classification?
questions.explanation: Species is the fundamental and smallest unit of biological classification.

questions.question: Which taxonomic rank comes directly above Genus?
questions.explanation: The hierarchy above Genus is Family. Several genera (plural of genus) make up a Family.

questions.question: Which kingdom do humans belong to?
questions.explanation: Humans belong to Kingdom Animalia because we are multicellular, heterotrophic, and mobile organisms.

questions.question: A mnemonic to remember the taxonomic hierarchy 'Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species' is:
options: Kids Play Computer Games On Friday Nights
Kangaroos Play Chess On Fine Grass Sand
Kings Play Chess On Fine Green Sand
Keep Plates Clean Or Family Gets Sick
questions.correctAnswer: Kings Play Chess On Fine Green Sand
questions.explanation: A common mnemonic is 'Kings Play Chess On Fine Green Sand' where each word starts with the same letter as a taxonomic rank.

questions.question: Which of the following classification levels contains the greatest number of species?
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the broadest and highest taxonomic rank and therefore contains the greatest diversity of organisms.

questions.question: The scientific name of the domestic dog is Canis familiaris. What is the genus name?
questions.explanation: In Canis familiaris, Canis is the genus name (capitalized) and familiaris is the species name (lowercase).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between organisms in the same genus?
options: They are closely related and share a recent common ancestor
questions.correctAnswer: They are closely related and share a recent common ancestor
questions.explanation: Organisms in the same genus are closely related and share many characteristics from a common ancestor.

questions.question: In early classification systems, Aristotle classified organisms into:
questions.explanation: Aristotle's early classification divided organisms into only two groups: plants and animals.

questions.question: What is the main limitation of using common names for organisms?
options: The same common name can refer to different species in different regions
questions.correctAnswer: The same common name can refer to different species in different regions
questions.explanation: Common names vary by language and region, causing confusion, which is why scientific names are preferred.

questions.question: Which taxonomic rank would contain organisms that are more diverse: Class or Order?
questions.explanation: Class is a broader rank than Order, so it contains more diverse groups of organisms.

questions.question: What feature do all members of Kingdom Plantae share?
options: They can photosynthesize and are autotrophic
questions.correctAnswer: They can photosynthesize and are autotrophic
questions.explanation: Plants are multicellular autotrophs that photosynthesize using chlorophyll to produce their own food.
